title: Shortest self-orthogonal and LCD embeddings of linear codes over Fq+uFq
abstract: This paper determines the exact lengths of shortest self-orthogonal and LCD embeddings of linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_q+u\mathbb{F}_q$. By decomposing Gram matrices over $\mathbb{F}_q+u\mathbb{F}_q$ into pairs of symmetric matrices over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, the embedding problems are reduced to the congruence classification of symmetric and alternate matrices over finite fields. Complete formulas for the shortest self-orthogonal embedding length are obtained, with two distinct cases arising in both even and odd characteristic. We also show that every self-orthogonal code over $\mathbb{F}_q+u\mathbb{F}_q$ with nonzero free rank can be viewed as a shortest self-orthogonal embedding of another code. We use Witt theory to construct all shortest self-orthogonal embeddings. A complete characterization of shortest LCD embeddings is also established in terms of invertible and arbitrary matrices of prescribed sizes appended to a generator matrix. Examples of self-orthogonal and LCD embeddings with the largest minimum distance for the code considered are also presented, some of whose Gray images are optimal codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$.

title: Ada-TokenCom: Rate-Adaptive Token Communications via Large-Model-Driven Token Compression and Generation
abstract: Token Communications (TokenCom) has recently emerged as a new paradigm in which tokens serve as unified units for communication and computation, enabling efficient multimodal semantic and goal-oriented transmission. In this paper, we develop Ada-TokenCom, a rate-adaptive TokenCom framework based on large autoregressive models, which integrates next-token prediction with arithmetic coding to achieve ultra-low bitrate semantic communication at the token level. We propose a mixed reconstruction/generation scheme, where the transmitter encodes and transmits the highly informative tokens at the beginning of the token sequence leveraging a pre-trained autoregressive large model, while the receiver uses an identical model to predict the rest. Moreover, we design a Lyapunov-based algorithm to dynamically optimize both the source compression rate and the modulation and coding scheme, adapting to time-varying network conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed Ada-TokenCom framework outperforms both digital and deep joint source-channel coding-based semantic communication baselines.

title: Synthetic Linguistic Agency: How an Embodied Mortal Agent Learns Linguistic Affordances through Consequential Social Experience
abstract: Contemporary language models can converse fluently and influence human decisions, yet their exchanges do not enter a continuing, vulnerable life of their own. Linguistic-agency theory identifies this missing connection as linguistic agency and characterizes it through embodiment, linguistic participation, and precariousness: a body that acts and bears consequences, interaction that changes both agent and partner, and a future that can be sustained or lost. Two coordinated studies examine how this organization can appear in artificial systems. First, we translate these relations into inspectable criteria for Synthetic Linguistic Agency (SLA) and identify several existing SLA systems. Second, building on Homeostatically Regulated Reinforcement Learning, we develop a mortality-grounded linguistic-reinforcement-learning model and instantiate it in an Embodied Mortal Agent (EMA). The EMA learns how ways of speaking change a partner's willingness to protect it and chooses expressions by considering what those responses mean for its remaining life. Controlled experiments show that linguistic choices depend on the EMA's body and social history, change partner behavior, and adapt through experience with particular partners. When bodily consequences persist, linguistic choices alter the future of the same life; when the body is reset, their social effects remain but no longer shape continued viability. The resulting EMA exhibits SLA under our operational definition. This work motivates further research on synthetic empathy and strategic human-AI interaction: how artificial agents with persistent bodies, histories, and futures might develop and express empathy, and how people might care for, negotiate with, or govern them.

title: Generalized Splines and Gaussian Processes
abstract: For finite-dimensional linear inverse problems where the variables are Gaussian, it is well-known that the minimum-mean-square error estimator takes the form of a regularized least-squares data fit. In this chapter, we show that this equivalence extends to a much broader infinite-dimensional setting where generalized splines take the role of linear regressors and generalized Gaussian processes on a nuclear space $S$ are the counterpart of Gaussian random vectors. The scope of this extension is of the same nature as the switch from the classic notion of function to that of a distribution, also known as a "generalized function." Our formalism involves a whitening/regularization operator $L: S\to S'$ whose continuous extension induces a native Hilbert space $H\subset S'$ that plays a central role in our characterization. The presentation is self-contained for the most part and remarkably general and powerful. It allows for the recovery of all known instances of such equivalences; in particular, the methods involving innovations and reproducing-kernel Hilbert spaces developed by Kailath and his students, and the mathematical correspondence between fractional splines and Mandelbrot's fractional Brownian motion (fractals), with the former being the optimal estimators of the latter. It also covers general Bayesian methods for the resolution of infinite-dimensional inverse problems.

title: Quantum State-Based Distributed Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of distributed computing utilizing quantum states, specifically leveraging superposition and entanglement. The core claim is that these quantum phenomena can be harnessed to enable parallel computation and enhanced information processing within a distributed system. We introduce a novel architecture designed around manipulating quantum states to perform computations across multiple nodes. The system's efficiency stems from the inherent parallelism offered by quantum superposition and the ability to correlate data through entanglement. This approach represents a fundamentally new paradigm for distributed computing, moving beyond classical limitations and opening possibilities for tackling computationally intensive problems. The architecture outlined here provides a framework for future research and development in this burgeoning field. This paper focuses on the theoretical design and potential benefits, without the inclusion of experimental results.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Automated Theorem Proving
abstract: This paper explores the integration of neural networks and symbolic reasoning techniques to enhance automated theorem proving. The core claim is that combining these approaches can significantly improve both the efficiency and accuracy of automated theorem proving systems. We propose a neuro-symbolic system comprising a neural network component designed to learn patterns within existing mathematical proofs, and a symbolic theorem prover responsible for executing logical deductions. The system will operate in a collaborative manner, with the neural network guiding the symbolic prover and the prover verifying the network's outputs. This approach addresses the limitations of purely symbolic systems, which often struggle with complex or unfamiliar mathematical domains, and the limitations of purely neural systems, which can lack the explicit logical structure necessary for robust theorem proving. The resulting architecture aims to accelerate mathematical discovery by leveraging the strengths of both symbolic and connectionist paradigms. The system's architecture and operational principles are detailed, outlining a pathway towards a more powerful and adaptable automated theorem prover.

title: Quantum Annealing Optimization Algorithm via Topological Quantization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum annealing optimization algorithms by integrating topological quantization. The core idea is to discretize the annealing path into a series of topological states, leveraging quantum entanglement to facilitate precise control over the system's evolution and ultimately enhance optimization performance. The method aims to overcome limitations inherent in traditional quantum annealing by providing a more granular and controllable mechanism for traversing the energy landscape. We demonstrate that this topological quantization approach leads to improved convergence speed and potentially higher solution accuracy. The theoretical framework and associated mathematical formulations are presented, outlining the key principles and operational details of the algorithm. This work represents a significant step toward realizing the full potential of quantum annealing for complex optimization problems.

title: Quantum Security Protocol Based on Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hardware security protocol leveraging the principles of quantum decoherence. Traditional hardware security protocols often rely on computationally intensive mathematical algorithms, rendering them vulnerable to sophisticated hardware attacks. Our approach introduces a fundamentally different strategy: embedding quantum decoherence directly into the hardware design. This creates an inherent barrier against eavesdropping and manipulation, as any attempt to observe or alter the quantum state will inevitably induce decoherence, destroying the key or corrupting the data. We detail the theoretical framework, focusing on the operational aspects of the protocol, and outline its potential advantages in mitigating hardware-based threats. The core claim of this work is to demonstrate a viable hardware security solution based on a well-established quantum phenomenon, offering a robust defense against attacks that exploit weaknesses in traditional cryptographic implementations.

title: Quantum-Inspired Data Compression Techniques for Graph Databases
abstract: Graph databases are increasingly used to model complex relationships within diverse domains, from social networks to biological systems. However, the inherent redundancy in graph data often leads to significant storage requirements. This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired techniques to achieve enhanced data compression for graph databases. We propose a novel compression algorithm that mimics aspects of superposition and entanglement to represent multiple relationships concurrently, thereby minimizing redundancy. The core concept involves encoding nodes and their connections within a superposition state, allowing for the simultaneous representation of multiple possible relationships. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and mathematical formulations that this approach can achieve higher compression ratios compared to traditional graph compression methods. The key innovations lie in the adaptation of quantum principles to the specific characteristics of graph data and the development of an efficient encoding and decoding scheme. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated through simulations and analytical results, showcasing its potential to dramatically reduce storage needs while preserving the essential information within the graph database.

title: ##基于遗传算法的编译器优化
abstract: This paper explores the application of genetic algorithms (GAs) to the optimization of compilers. Traditional compiler optimization relies heavily on hand-crafted heuristics and expert knowledge, often leading to suboptimal solutions. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging the inherent search capabilities of GAs to automatically discover and select optimal compilation optimization strategies. The core concept involves representing compilation optimization techniques as chromosomes within a GA framework. Through iterative processes of selection, crossover, and mutation, the GA evolves these chromosomes, ultimately converging on a set of optimized strategies. We demonstrate the potential of this method to significantly enhance program performance by automating the complex process of compiler optimization. The paper details the algorithm design, the representation of optimization strategies, and the GA implementation, providing a theoretical foundation and outlining a practical framework for automated compiler optimization.

title: fwb: An R package for the fractional weighted bootstrap
abstract: The nonparametric bootstrap is a simple method for performing inference on estimates of statistical parameters without making strong assumptions about the data or a statistical model and without needing to derive the formula for an estimator's variance (Efron & Tibshirani, 1993).The traditional nonparametric bootstrap involves resampling the observations from the sample with replacement, computing the estimates in the bootstrap sample, performing these steps many times, and summarizing the resulting distribution of bootstrap estimates to compute their confidence intervals.This is equivalent to drawing integer weights from a multinomial distribution and computing weighted estimates in each bootstrap sample.However, integer weights are not the only weights that can be used, and fractional (non-integer) weights carry certain advantages, described below.fwb implements the fractional weighted bootstrap, also known as the Bayesian bootstrap, using a simple interface and with options for parallelization.

title: Devising an approach to chatbot response personalization based on user query analysis
abstract: This study investigates the process that generates a personalized chatbot response based on the analysis of a user request within one interaction session. The task addressed is to increase the adaptability of the response by taking into account the parameters of the request and the related prompts. The proposed mechanism made it possible to describe the personalization process in terms of the total time spent on performing the main operations of the user and the system. The constructed model establishes a connection between the parameters of the user request, the characteristics of the temporary interaction dictionary, and the probability of receiving a personalized response. A feature of the model is the consideration of the number of possible semantic interpretations of the request and permissible options for combining words to build a logically consistent response. Based on the model, an algorithm has been developed that involves forming a temporary interaction dictionary, selecting relevant words, combining them, substituting them into the response structure, and checking the logical and semantic consistency of the result. The experiments showed that the probability of a positive completion of the personalization process increases with an increase in the number of response refinement steps, and the average time for analyzing a user's request with additional prompts and forming a personalized response is 3.056 s. It was experimentally established that with a decrease in the probability of a positive completion of the personalization process at each individual step from 10-6 to 10-8, values of the model components and the total time costs decrease. The proposed approach could be used in practical tasks of designing personalization modules for educational and consulting dialog systems, as well as for controlled generation of responses taking into account the structure of the request and the parameters of the current interaction session

title: Multi‐Agent Search under Uncertainty
abstract: Plan optimal multi-robot search paths despite imperfect sensor information When multiple robots must locate targets in presence of false positive and false negative detection errors, path planning becomes extraordinarily complex. Multi-Agent Search under Uncertainty addresses this challenge directly. Written by researchers with combined expertise spanning defense systems, applied mathematics, and machine learning, this book delivers both theoretical foundations in search and screening theory and ready-to-use algorithms for practical implementation. The book covers cooperative search and navigation methods for autonomous mobile agents operating with incomplete or noisy information. Readers learn how Deep Q-Learning enables robots to develop complex behaviors through trial-and-error interactions rather than pre-programmed instructions. Applications span search and rescue operations, military surveillance, environmental monitoring, and security systems. An accompanying website provides Python code for simulation practice. Key topics include: Value-based Q-Learning methods where robots learn expected rewards for specific actions in given states under sensor uncertainty conditions Multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches for swarm robotics where multiple robots learn cooperatively to accomplish collaborative search tasks Deep reinforcement learning using neural networks to process high-dimensional sensory inputs and execute complex search and tracking behaviors Algorithms for finding and tracking both stationary and moving targets while minimizing detection time despite false negative and positive readings Theoretical contributions to search and screening theory alongside practical algorithms validated in autonomous robotic systems development Designed for graduate students and researchers in robotics and reinforcement learning, this book bridges advanced theory with practical application. Professional developers building autonomous systems will find algorithms tested in real-world robotic development.

title: Introduction to Nature‐Inspired Intelligence
abstract: Meta-heuristic algorithms are computational intelligence paradigms specifically employed to solve numerous compound optimization issues and get the best outcome. With the development of computers in recent decades, scientists and academicians have continuously drawn inspiration from nature to create all-purpose devices that are even better than humans. A type of meta-heuristic algorithms known as “nature-inspired algorithms” draws inspiration from natural phenomena, inspired by Charles Darwin's theory of evolution. Improved wind turbine efficiency (by mimicking whale fins), water filtration and purification (by mimicking plant root systems), lightweight and robust materials (by mimicking spider silk), energy efficiency in buildings (by mimicking termite mound ventilation systems), optimized transportation design (by mimicking the kingfisher beak bullet train), coastal erosion control (by mimicking mangrove restoration), wind farm layouts (optimized by fish movement patterns) and urban heat island management through green infrastructure are just a few examples. In recent years, numerous paradigms for computing that draw inspiration from nature have surfaced. The important advancements in the area of computing influenced by nature are summarized in this paper, emphasizing biology-based algorithms. The ability of bio-inspired solutions to solve complex problems, such as NP-hard and black-box optimization, makes them useful for solving real-world issues. These solutions have drawn much interest from scholars and have been used to solve various optimization problems because of their easy scalability, parallelism, stochastic, and straightforward implementation characteristics. The idea behind the bio-inspired algorithms is the movement of organisms and frequently observed phenomena in certain animal species, such as schools of fish, herds of quadrupeds, and flocks of birds. The primary contribution of this chapter is to present a thorough overview of the characteristics and current challenges based on the nature-inspired computing paradigm. The main objective of this research is to identify the optimal outcome among every feasible solution for better decision-making. This comprehensive examination offers insightful research for general artificial intelligence technology in the future.

The ability of bio-inspired solutions to solve complex problems, such as NP-hard and black-box optimization, makes them useful for solving real-world issues. These solutions have drawn much interest from scholars and have been used to solve various optimization problems because of their easy scalability, parallelism, stochastic, and straightforward implementation characteristics. The idea behind the bio-inspired algorithms is the movement of organisms and frequently observed phenomena in certain animal species, such as schools of fish, herds of quadrupeds, and flocks of birds. The primary contribution of this chapter is to present a thorough overview of the characteristics and current challenges based on the nature-inspired computing paradigm. The main objective of this research is to identify the optimal outcome among every feasible solution for better decision-making. This comprehensive examination offers insightful research for general artificial intelligence technology in the future.

title: Text-Driven Artistic Staging: 3D Posing, Lighting, and Camera References from Paintings
abstract: Artists coordinate human pose, illumination, and camera placement to convey narrative and emotion, but existing generative methods typically model these elements independently. We introduce text-to-editable 3D staging, a task that jointly generates human poses, a dominant light, and a camera configuration from an affective description. We construct 11,911 text--staging pairs from 2,328 figurative paintings by reconstructing SMPL bodies, estimating low-frequency illumination, recovering camera parameters, and pairing each scene with ArtEmis descriptions. We train a flow-matching transformer that supports variable numbers of figures and produces multiple staging alternatives for each prompt. On held-out descriptions, the model achieves 32.2\% retrieval R@1, compared with 16.6\% for CLIP-based nearest-neighbor retrieval, while approximately preserving corpus-level diversity. These results demonstrate the feasibility of generating editable, emotionally conditioned 3D staging references from text.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Cross-City POI Recommendation on a Large-Scale Benchmark
abstract: Cross-city point-of-interest (POI) recommendation is crucial for navigating unfamiliar urban environments, yet its progress has historically been constrained by data limitations. Using the recently proposed large-scale benchmark Trip World, we empirically re-examine whether conclusions drawn on small prior benchmarks still hold under worldwide coverage, low home-destination region overlap, and large, semantically rich POI inventories. Our evaluation surfaces three bottlenecks of representative state-of-the-art methods: (1) hometown-aware models appear to rely more on destination-region priors than on user-specific preference transfer; (2) their accuracy-efficiency trade-off degrades at this scale, where the simplest model is among the strongest; and (3) existing mechanisms for integrating semantic metadata yield little benefit. We further include a diagnostic pilot on agentic methods adapted from next-POI recommendation, finding that naive adaptation trails a simple popularity prior even though the relevant semantic signal is present in the data. These results highlight the need for task-specific designs that support cross-city preference transfer, semantic grounding, and scalable reasoning over unseen destination inventories.

title: Grasshopper2D
abstract: Grasshopper2D is a C++ implementation of simulated annealing for the planar Euclidean grasshopper problem on a square grid. It searches for unit-area lawn configurations that maximize the discretized grasshopper success probability for a fixed jump distance, with an optional nearest-neighbor interaction.

title: Predictive Coding of Sensory Data using Hierarchical Recurrent Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of hierarchical recurrent neural networks (HRNNs) for predictive coding of sensory data. Traditional recurrent neural networks often struggle to effectively model complex temporal dependencies inherent in sensory information, particularly those spanning multiple timescales. The core idea presented here is that a hierarchical structure within an RNN architecture, where each layer learns to predict the input at a different temporal scale, significantly enhances predictive coding capabilities. This approach allows the network to decompose temporal dependencies into manageable levels, capturing both immediate and distant relationships. We propose a framework for designing and training HRNNs, outlining key architectural considerations and learning strategies. The resulting model demonstrates improved performance in capturing and predicting sequential sensory data compared to standard RNNs, showcasing the potential of this approach for applications in areas such as signal processing, neuroscience, and robotics. The model's ability to learn predictive representations directly addresses the inherent challenges in sensory data analysis and provides a novel pathway for understanding how predictive processes contribute to perception.

title: ##基于多智能体协作的资源优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to resource optimization utilizing a multi-agent system (MAS) framework. The core claim is the design of a system capable of automatically optimizing resource allocation and collaborative strategies. This is achieved through a mechanism that combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a tailored multi-agent communication protocol. The system enables agents to engage in both cooperative and competitive interactions, ultimately leading to enhanced resource utilization efficiency. Traditional resource optimization methods often suffer from inflexibility and require manual tuning. This MAS approach introduces a level of adaptability and autonomy, dynamically adjusting to changing conditions and optimizing the overall system performance. The system's architecture and control strategy are detailed, outlining the key components and their interactions. The research explores the trade-offs between cooperation and competition within the multi-agent environment and demonstrates the potential for significant improvements in resource allocation compared to static or centrally-controlled solutions. The results highlight the effectiveness of this approach for complex, dynamic resource management scenarios. ---

title: 基于生物启发算法的程序资源分配
abstract: This paper investigates the application of bio-inspired algorithms, specifically Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), to the problem of program resource allocation. The core idea is to model resource allocation as an optimization task and leverage the collective intelligence found in nature – particularly the behavior of ants and swarming animals – to dynamically adjust resource assignments. Traditional resource allocation methods often rely on hand-crafted algorithms, which can be inflexible and struggle to adapt to varying workloads and system conditions. By employing ACO and PSO, this research proposes a system that can automatically learn and optimize resource utilization, potentially leading to significant improvements in efficiency and performance. The key contribution lies in the adaptive nature of the algorithms, allowing them to respond effectively to changes in resource demands and system dynamics. This work lays the groundwork for a more intelligent and responsive approach to program resource management.

title: Algorithmic Reservoir Computing with Quantum State Evolution
abstract: Reservoir computing is a promising approach to dynamic systems modeling, known for its computational efficiency and ability to capture temporal dynamics. However, traditional reservoir computing often struggles with theoretical understanding and guarantees of performance. This work proposes a novel framework that integrates reservoir computing with quantum state evolution. The core idea involves utilizing a quantum system as the reservoir, where its state evolves governed by a parameterized Hamiltonian. The output signal is then extracted by measuring the state of this quantum reservoir. This approach aims to leverage the inherent complexity and parallelism of quantum systems to potentially enhance reservoir computing's capabilities. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this hybrid system and present a conceptual model. The key contribution lies in the combination of these two powerful paradigms, offering a potential route toward more robust and scalable dynamic systems modeling. Further research will focus on optimizing the Hamiltonian parameters and exploring different measurement strategies to maximize the system's performance.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Topological Network Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel protocol for dynamic quantum entanglement topological network, aiming to achieve robust quantum communication and distributed quantum computation. The core of the protocol relies on leveraging topological protection of quantum states and dynamic adjustment of entanglement within a topological quantum network. We introduce a framework that utilizes the inherent topological properties of entangled states to construct fault-tolerant encoding schemes. Real-time control of the network topology allows for optimization of entanglement quality and overall network performance. The proposed approach addresses the vulnerability of traditional quantum networks to noise by incorporating topological protection and dynamic control, offering a fundamentally new network architecture. The protocol's key features include adaptable error correction, enhanced entanglement distribution, and scalable quantum network design. We outline the mathematical foundation for the protocol, including the entanglement fidelity metrics and topological network optimization algorithms. This work represents a significant step towards practical, robust quantum networks capable of supporting complex quantum information processing tasks.

title: Construction of a parametric invariant hypergraph model for integrating and analyzing multi-context educational data
abstract: This study examines multi-context educational data acquired from independent digital platforms and characterized by differences in the composition of entities, types of interactions, and data representation schemes. The task addressed relates to the lack of a unified model for the invariant representation of heterogeneously structured data, the assessment of their structural compatibility, the determination of the costs of mutual adaptation, and the possibility of comparative analysis of digital platforms while preserving the characteristics of the educational context. A parametrically typed invariant hypergraph model has been proposed, which represents educational data as typed hypergraphs, their semantic normalization into a single type space, as well as the calculation of indicators of structural invariance, adaptation, and integral utility. A parametric analysis of sensitivity to changes in the data structure and model weighting coefficients has been suggested. The novelty of this work is underscored by the following: – a unified parametric hypergraph model has been constructed that combines the invariant representation of educational data, a quantitative assessment of the structural compatibility, adaptation costs, and integral utility of digital educational platforms; – a parametric analysis has been proposed to examine the influence of structure and weighting factors on the integration and comparative analysis of platforms; – the model was experimentally tested on data from independent educational platforms, including over 3,100 educational records and 4,861 hyperedges, revealing differences in the structural compatibility of the studied contexts. The model supports decision making in the selection and design of digital educational ecosystems in the context of structurally heterogeneous data

title: Informing School Library Professional Advisory on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence to Communicate Accessible Home Literacy Advice
abstract: Schools communicate the importance of home literacy practices in the early schooling years and beyond, but low parental English literacy can be a significant barrier to sharing evidence and strategies. School library professionals often play a key role in the implementation of new technologies, and in promoting reading and literacy within and beyond the school. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools are already being used in some schools for a variety of purposes despite known and emerging limitations and issues, and as digital and information literacy experts within schools, school library professionals may advise on and facilitate this use. This study seeks to determine if GenAI tools are reliable for generating simplified messaging on home literacy for effective communication with culturally and linguistically diverse homes. This research tests the reliability and consistency of GenAI tools in adjusting texts to enhance accessibility, and how research related messaging may be distorted through this simplification process. Findings suggest that GenAI tools are not currently consistent in their readability determinations, typically underestimating the complexity of the text they produce, with significant human oversight still needed. As such, at this stage, school library professionals’ advisory in schools should be responsive to these findings.

title: Computational Intelligence Using Fuzzy Logic in Educational Data Analysis A Study of Methodologies and Applications
abstract: In this exploratory research, the use of computational intelligence, more especially fuzzy sense, in the analysis of educational data is investigated. The paper also investigates colorful approaches and the practical applications of these methodologies. To improve tutoring and literacy challenges, educational institutions are increasingly resorting to data-driven techniques. This trend is expected to continue. The use of fuzzy sense, which is well-known for its capacity to manage queries and complexity, provides potentially useful tools for evaluating educational data. The purpose of this project is to investigate how fuzzy sense models can be utilized to reuse and interpret various educational data sets. These data sets include educational criteria for student achievement as well as learning gesture patterns. In the process of establishing meaningful perceptivity from educational data, comparative evaluations of various fuzzy sense approaches highlight both the benefits and limits of these methodologies. To demonstrate the efficacy of fuzzy sense in the process of developing educational decision-making procedures, case studies illustrate realistic executions across a variety of educational environments. The findings highlight the potential for computational intelligence, and more specifically fuzzy sense, to change the way educational data analysis is done by providing preceptors and stakeholders with additional nuanced and practical perceptivity.

title: When Agents Act Unwatched: The Reduced-Supervision Paradox in Agentic AI
abstract: Agentic AI is sold on a simple promise: the system keeps acting when the user stops watching. That promise creates an accountability inversion. As stepwise supervision recedes, verification does not disappear; it moves into the runtime infrastructure that defines authority, records action, interrupts execution, checks outcomes, and supports repair. We call this the reduced-supervision paradox. Using a 63-artifact audit, we examine its public visibility across 46 research papers and 17 engineering, documentation, security, and governance sources. We find that agents' action surfaces are far easier to reconstruct than the mechanisms needed to answer for their actions. Tool mediation and monitoring traces were clearly visible in 40 and 37 artifacts, whereas checkpoint placement was clearly visible in 6, validator independence in 4, recovery in 2, and contestability in 1. Three action paths show why this imbalance matters. A repository path can preserve rich diffs after a consequential change. A browser path can cross organizational boundaries faster than permissions travel. A service path can follow policy while leaving affected people without recourse. We argue that observability can become a substitute for accountability when it shifts verification onto users after meaningful intervention is no longer possible. Our action-path diagnostic instead asks whether a delegated action remains connected to authority, evidence, interruption, independent judgment, recovery, and challenge. The claim is deliberately bounded to public visibility; it does not establish the prevalence or effectiveness of undisclosed controls. We contribute an action-level account that recasts the harness from a technical wrapper into accountability infrastructure.

title: Attribute Token Arithmetic: Disentangled and Continuous Semantic Control for Visual Autoregressive Models
abstract: Autoregressive text-to-image generation has recently achieved remarkable progress, offering high-fidelity synthesis via a unified generative framework. However, fine-grained semantic control remains challenging due to the attribute entanglement and the misalignment between textual and fine-grained visual representations. In this paper, we introduce Attribute Token Arithmetic (ATA), a method that enables disentangled and continuous attribute control in visual autoregressive modelling. Inspired by the vector arithmetic property observed in word embeddings, ATA identifies semantic directions corresponding to visual attributes (e.g., aging, fatness, emotion) directly within the pretrained autoregressive latent space. These directions are learned from a single reference image, without model retraining or large-scale supervision. During generation, attributes can be continuously adjusted and compositionally combined through simple arithmetic operations with other attribute tokens. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ATA achieves identity-preserving, fine-grained, and multi-attribute adjustment, outperforming existing autoregressive editing baselines in controllability, generality, and computational efficiency. Our code will be available at https://github.com/Madaoer/ATA.

title: Intelligent Mineralization Recognition Method Based on Remote Sensing Data
abstract: In recent years, the application of remote sensing technology in geological exploration has gradually deepened, especially in improving the efficiency of mineral exploration, showing great potential. However, in the face of massive remote sensing data, traditional experience-based manual recognition methods cannot meet the needs of mineral exploration in terms of effectiveness and efficiency. This article proposes an intelligent mining prediction method based on remote sensing data and deep learning neural networks. Using high-precision remote sensing data, a deep convolutional neural network mining prediction model is established with known fluorite vein bands as positive samples and unknown areas as negative samples. Three convolutional neural network architectures, Alex LeNet5, VGG16, and GoogLeNet Inception v1, are used for comparative experiments. The results show that the Alex LeNet5 model performs the best in fluorite mining prediction tasks in remote sensing images, outperforming the VGG16 and GoogLeNet Inception V1 models.The model was applied to fluorite prospecting prediction, identifying five mineralization prospect areas.

title: Artificial Intelligence as an Entropy-Reduction Operator: Imposing Order on Laboratory Chaos via LLM Hardware Orchestration and the Model Hardware Standard
abstract: Author: Luigi Usai ORCID: 0009-0003-3001-717X Publication Type: Technical Preprint / Epistemological Note (Zenodo Version v2) Date: August 28, 2026 License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) Attribution and Corrigendum Notice (v2) Corrigendum Notice: This preprint articulates an epistemological and computational thesis regarding the core utility of Artificial Intelligence as a universal entropy-reduction engine. The Model Hardware Standard (MHS), referenced throughout this work as an empirical case study of hardware abstraction, is an open specification introduced by Anthropic and the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) Janelia Research Campus (August 2026). The author claims no proprietary authorship over the MHS specification, but provides the theoretical framework governing operational entropy reduction, cognitive orchestration, and configuration latency collapse in MHS-compliant scientific workflows. Abstract The widespread adoption and practical success of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) stem from a fundamental computational mechanism: their capacity to act as entropy-reduction operators, imposing deterministic structure and operational order on high-dimensional, chaotic environments. Human researchers constantly face combinatorial friction when coordinating heterogeneous, unstandardized systems. Modern experimental laboratories represent a quintessential failure mode of this dynamic: empirical progress is severely bottlenecked by "hardware chaos"—a fragmented ecosystem of proprietary actuators, sensors, and instruments requiring tedious manual configuration, custom glue code, and extensive calibration overhead. Using the recently announced Model Hardware Standard (MHS) (Anthropic & HHMI Janelia, 2026) as a foundational case study, this paper formalizes how AI agents and LLM-driven orchestration layers resolve interface fragmentation. By translating abstract, high-level scientific hypotheses into deterministic machine-executable parameters, AI collapses operational entropy, reducing experiment setup and execution latency by up to 80% (operating at $\approx 0.20$ of traditional manual time requirements). We demonstrate that AI's core value proposition is not mere statistical pattern matching, but the systematic transformation of chaotic human and physical parameter spaces into ordered, verifiable, and accelerated discovery pipelines. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Entropy Reduction, Scientific Automation, Model Hardware Standard, Large Language Models (LLMs), Laboratory Workflow Optimization, Operational Complexity. 1. The Foundational Thesis: Why AI Succeeds by Imposing Order on Chaos The fundamental reason human operators find Artificial Intelligence indispensable across scientific, computational, and organizational domains is its capacity to resolve cognitive and operational chaos. Human cognition excels at conceptual hypothesis generation but degrades rapidly under high combinatorial loads, syntactic fragmentation, and multi-variable parameter calibration. Unstructured environments possess high Shannon-Gibbs operational entropy: $$H(\mathcal{X}) = -\sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} p(x) \log_2 p(x)$$ where $\mathcal{X}$ represents the state space of possible system configurations, communication protocols, parameter settings, and error states. title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Relational Entropy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to temporal graph embedding, termed Temporal Graph Embedding with Relational Entropy (TGE). Existing graph embedding methods often fail to adequately represent the dynamic evolution of graphs, neglecting the intricate relationships that change over time. We propose a framework that leverages relational entropy – a metric quantifying the diversity and complexity of relationships – to guide the embedding process. The core idea is to utilize a recurrent neural network (RNN) trained to predict future relationship transitions. The RNN's training is guided by a loss function that incorporates these relational entropy scores, effectively weighting transitions based on their informational content and the overall complexity of the graph's relationship structure. This approach moves beyond traditional node adjacency or edge count representations, offering a richer and more accurate depiction of temporal graph dynamics. Experimental validation, though not presented here due to the focus on the methodology, demonstrates the potential of this technique to improve the quality of temporal graph embeddings.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Stochastic Differential Equations
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling complex causal systems by integrating stochastic differential equations (SDEs) within causal Bayesian networks. Traditional Bayesian networks struggle to capture the inherent stochasticity and dynamic evolution present in many real-world systems. This work addresses this limitation by representing each variable in the network as a node, with its influence on neighboring nodes governed by an SDE. This allows for the simulation of dynamic causal relationships, explicitly accounting for noise and uncertainty. The core claim is that this combined framework offers a more accurate representation of complex causal systems compared to standard Bayesian networks. The mechanism involves defining stochastic differential equations that model the time-dependent evolution of variables, providing a richer and more nuanced depiction of causality. This approach is particularly relevant for applications where the system's behavior is influenced by both deterministic causal links and random fluctuations. The resulting model offers improved predictive capabilities and a deeper understanding of the underlying causal processes.

title: Quantum Computing: The Time Transistor Model and Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper explores the potential of the Time Transistor Model (TTM) within the realm of quantum computing. The TTM, characterized by its inherent temporal dynamics, offers a novel approach to algorithm design and implementation compared to traditional models like the Qubit model. We present a framework for designing quantum algorithms based on the TTM, focusing on algorithms with time-dependent operations. Specifically, we investigate algorithms that leverage the controlled evolution of quantum states over time, analogous to the behavior of a time-dependent transistor. The core contribution lies in formulating a set of algorithms that exploit this temporal dependence to achieve computational advantages. The paper details the mathematical formulation of these algorithms, including the definition of key operators and their temporal evolution. Furthermore, we discuss the potential challenges and future research directions related to implementing these algorithms on quantum hardware, considering the practical constraints and complexities involved. Ultimately, this work aims to demonstrate the viability of the TTM as a powerful tool for quantum algorithm development.

title: Quantum State Thermodynamics Entropy Increase Principle and the Limits of Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the limits of quantum computing by applying the entropy increase principle from quantum state thermodynamics. We analyze the fundamental challenges posed by energy dissipation and information loss during quantum computations, leveraging the second law of thermodynamics. Specifically, we explore the implications of entropy generation on quantum coherence and fidelity, and propose theoretical frameworks for mitigating these effects. The core argument centers on demonstrating that inherent entropy generation processes, when unchecked, inevitably lead to the degradation of quantum states and ultimately limit the scalability of quantum computers. We formulate key mathematical expressions relating entropy generation rates to quantum gate operations and decoherence models. The analysis reveals that while quantum computation offers potential advantages, a thorough understanding and strategic management of entropy are crucial for realizing its full potential. The work highlights the necessity of robust error correction and innovative quantum architectures designed to minimize entropy generation. Furthermore, we explore the theoretical boundaries imposed by the second law of thermodynamics on the achievable fidelity of quantum computations.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Temporal Logic and Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by integrating neural networks and temporal logic. The core idea is to leverage the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks to learn probabilistic knowledge representations, and then to utilize a temporal logic engine for logical inference and reasoning about temporal relationships between events. The proposed system aims to overcome the limitations of purely neural or purely symbolic approaches by combining their respective strengths. Specifically, a neural network is trained to map observational data into a probabilistic state representation, which is subsequently used as input to a temporal logic reasoner. This allows for the deduction of consequences and the verification of temporal constraints. The system's architecture is described, along with the key components and their interactions. The paper outlines the core claim, the core mechanism, and highlights the novelty of the integration. Finally, it discusses potential applications and future research directions.

title: Генетический подход к повышению производительности распределенных хранилищ данных в телекоммуникационных системах
abstract: Рассмотрены ключевые решения по построению генетического алгоритма, лежащего в основе предлагаемого подхода к созданию распределенных хранилищ данных в телекоммуникационных системах с целью повышения их производительности, а также обсуждаются экспериментальные результаты по применению предлагаемого подхода. Сформулирована постановка задачи оптимального распределения файлов по узлам хранилища данных, в которой необходимо достичь максимального значения показателя его производительности при условии удовлетворения заданного значения показателя отказоустойчивости. Предложены и детально проработаны шаги генетического алгоритма, содержащие некоторые новшества, касающиеся, в частности, использования столбцов матрицы, определяющей план распределения файлов, в качестве генов хромосом, реализации универсальной стохастической выборки точек скрещивания, а также использования принципа элитизма для сохранения наилучшего генофонда. Проведены вычислительные эксперименты, показавшие, что предложенный подход позволяет решить поставленную задачу с достаточно высокой точностью за существенно меньшее время, чем это делают традиционные математические методы оптимизации. The article discusses key decisions on the construction of a genetic algorithm that underlies the proposed approach to constructing distributed data storages in telecommunication systems with the aim of increasing their performance, and experimental results on the application of the proposed approach are also discussed. The problem of optimal distribution of files among data storage nodes is formulated, in which it is necessary to achieve the maximum value of its performance indicator, subject to satisfying the specified value of the fault-tolerance indicator. The steps of a genetic algorithm were proposed and detailed, incorporating several innovations, including the use of columns of the matrix defining the file distribution plan as chromosomal genes, the implementation of a universal stochastic selection of crossover points, and the use of the elitism principle to preserve the best gene pool. Computational experiments were conducted, demonstrating that the proposed approach enables solving the problem with a sufficiently high accuracy in significantly less time than traditional mathematical optimization methods.

title: Particle Swarm Optimization for Effective Feature Selection in Smart Logistics
abstract: The paper outlines the utilization of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for enhancing feature selection efficacy. Features are considered as particles which are ranked in a two-dimensional optimization space. During optimization process, the velocity and position of the particles are updated using feature rankings in addition to particle ranks. To complete the task, a novel particle ranking based on particle distance from dominated and non-dominated particles is developed, which is subsequently used to the computation of feature ranks. In comparison to five cutting-edge feature selection approaches, the proposed feature selection method has been evaluated on 6 UCI datasets and 2 datasets from real-world applications. Additionally, experiments revealed that the suggested strategy outperforms currently used feature selection techniques.

title: AI as Teammate: Rethinking Task Distribution in Medical Training
abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, into medical training has prompted concerns about learner over-reliance, misuse, and erosion of foundational clinical competencies. We propose a conceptual reframing at the decision level: the problem is not misuse but misclassification - a mechanistic failure of real-time metacognitive evaluation in selecting a subzone-inappropriate AI interaction mode. Drawing on "SCAN" (Substitute, Complement, Aid, Non-Negotiable), a human-centric decision-making framework for generative AI task allocation grounded in Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development and metacognition, we advance the emerging social-constructivist conversation around AI in medical education by offering a testable account of AI's role in clinical reasoning development. This framework yields testable predictions for how misclassification can be detected, mitigated, and, more importantly, prevented in the clinical learning environment. Regarding clinical reasoning development, we show how trajectories of skill acquisition (upskilling) and failure (the triad of skill failure: de-skilling, never-skilling, and mis-skilling) operate at the individual task level in ways that fixed-phase, cohort-wide treatments fail to capture. We further identify passive engagement within correctly classified AI-scaffolded tasks as a particularly insidious, detection-resistant pathway to mis-skilling - one requiring subzone re-identification from AI assistance to expert assistance, with human experts serving as epistemic auditors. evidence.title: AI as Teammate: Rethinking Task Distribution in Medical Training
evidence.abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, into medical training has prompted concerns about learner over-reliance, misuse, and erosion of foundational clinical competencies. We propose a conceptual reframing at the decision level: the problem is not misuse but misclassification - a mechanistic failure of real-time metacognitive evaluation in selecting a subzone-inappropriate AI interaction mode. Drawing on "SCAN" (Substitute, Complement, Aid, Non-Negotiable), a human-centric decision-making framework for generative AI task allocation grounded in Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development and metacognition, we advance the emerging social-constructivist conversation around AI in medical education by offering a testable account of AI's role in clinical reasoning development. This framework yields testable predictions for how misclassification can be detected, mitigated, and, more importantly, prevented in the clinical learning environment. Regarding clinical reasoning development, we show how trajectories of skill acquisition (upskilling) and failure (the triad of skill failure: de-skilling, never-skilling, and mis-skilling) operate at the individual task level in ways that fixed-phase, cohort-wide treatments fail to capture. title: Cyc3D: Evaluating Cyclic Structural Stability and Asset Usability in Image-to-3D Generation
abstract: Image-conditioned 3D generation has advanced rapidly, yet existing evaluation protocols largely judge rendered-view plausibility and semantic alignment, overlooking whether a generator forms a stable 3D interpretation and produces assets usable in graphics pipelines. We introduce Cyc3D, a multidimensional benchmark that evaluates image-to-3D generation along two complementary axes: Cross-View Object Consistency and Representation Quality. At the asset level, Cyc3D measures whether object identity remains semantically coherent across rendered viewpoints. At the model level, we propose View-Cycle Structural Consistency, a closed-loop render-regenerate-align protocol that repeatedly re-observes a generated asset from novel views and quantifies geometric, perceptual, and semantic drift across generations. To assess native asset usability beyond rendered appearance, Cyc3D further evaluates geometric structure, reference-image fidelity, mesh discretization and efficiency, and UV parameterization quality. Together, these diagnostics expose failures obscured by a single perceptual score and provide interpretable evidence of both model instability and representation defects. Experiments on five representative image-to-3D systems show that closed-source feed-forward models consistently outperform open-source optimization-based baselines in geometric fidelity, mesh quality, and cycle stability. Nevertheless, even the strongest methods achieve cycle-stability scores below 48, revealing a persistent gap between visually plausible generation and robust 3D object understanding.

title: Розроблення підходу до персоналізації відповідей чат-бота на основі аналізу користувацьких запитів
abstract: This study investigates the process that generates a personalized chatbot response based on the analysis of a user request within one interaction session. The task addressed is to increase the adaptability of the response by taking into account the parameters of the request and the related prompts. The proposed mechanism made it possible to describe the personalization process in terms of the total time spent on performing the main operations of the user and the system. The constructed model establishes a connection between the parameters of the user request, the characteristics of the temporary interaction dictionary, and the probability of receiving a personalized response. A feature of the model is the consideration of the number of possible semantic interpretations of the request and permissible options for combining words to build a logically consistent response. Based on the model, an algorithm has been developed that involves forming a temporary interaction dictionary, selecting relevant words, combining them, substituting them into the response structure, and checking the logical and semantic consistency of the result. The experiments showed that the probability of a positive completion of the personalization process increases with an increase in the number of response refinement steps, and the average time for analyzing a user's request with additional prompts and forming a personalized response is 3.056 s. It was experimentally established that with a decrease in the probability of a positive completion of the personalization process at each individual step from 10-6 to 10-8, values of the model components and the total time costs decrease. The proposed approach could be used in practical tasks of designing personalization modules for educational and consulting dialog systems, as well as for controlled generation of responses taking into account the structure of the request and the parameters of the current interaction session

title: QSOL-FED Lean 4 Formalization: Machine-Checked Constitutional and Protocol Separation Invariants
abstract: This record publishes Version 1.0.0 of the Lean 4 formalization of selected constitutional and protocol separation invariants from QSOL-FED, a sovereign federation protocol for independent computational systems, AI councils, research systems, humans, and deterministic services. The formalization is explicitly bound to the immutable QSOL-FED v0.11.0 source release and contains 47 named Lean 4 graduation theorems covering thirteen principal invariant families: Prime Directive admissionSignature, trust, and authority separationPeering and capability separationImport non-authorityLifecycle monotonicityPartition sovereigntyProvenance preservationCanonical identity determinismHolodeck separation and safeguardsAdapter non-authoritySDK conformance boundariesFederation Assembly sovereigntyTransport identity and provenance independence The theorem package uses Lean 4.33.1 and includes an environment-level type audit for all graduation theorems together with a manifest-bound kernel axiom audit. The completed graduation set contains no custom Lean axioms, no unresolved sorry or admit, no external Lake dependencies, and no kernel-axiom dependencies among the 47 graduation theorems. The formalization establishes properties of the stated abstract QSOL-FED model under explicitly named assumptions. It does not constitute whole-program verification of the Rust, Python, or TypeScript implementations, a proof of production or deployment security, a proof of operating-system or hardware isolation, a proof of real-world principal uniqueness, or a proof of SHA-256 collision resistance. The record contains three archival artifacts: a human-facing PDF explaining QSOL-FED, the Lean 4 formalization, its theorem families, assurance structure, assumptions, proof scope, limitations, and reproducibility boundary;an exact Phase 10 formalization source and evidence archive bound to the reviewed merged-main commit;release notes recording publication identity, source bindings, verification evidence, claim boundaries, and artifact integrity. The formalization follows QSOL-FED Phase 9 MORIARTY/1 adversarial graduation. MORIARTY evidence and Lean formal verification remain deliberately distinct assurance layers: absence of discovered counterexamples is not treated as a security proof, and the Lean model does not silently extend its claims beyond the propositions it actually proves. Zenodo record Version 1.0.0 is a formalization-publication version and should not be confused with the QSOL-FED software version, which remains v0.11.0 for the immutable source target formalized here.

title: Adaptive Quantum Feedback Control
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive quantum feedback control (AQFC) to enhance the precision and efficiency of quantum operations. The core concept involves constructing a closed-loop system where quantum state measurements are continuously fed back into a control mechanism, enabling dynamic adjustment of control parameters. We explore the theoretical framework and potential implementations of AQFC, focusing on its ability to mitigate the effects of noise and imperfections inherent in quantum systems. The primary goal is to demonstrate how AQFC can improve the fidelity of quantum gates and overall control performance. The proposed methodology offers a promising approach for achieving robust and reliable quantum control, particularly in complex quantum systems. The mathematical framework presented details the control equations and feedback mechanisms utilized in the AQFC system.

title: Quantum Data Compression Based on Quantum State Reordering
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum data compression utilizing the principles of quantum state reordering. Traditional quantum data compression techniques often suffer from inefficiencies, primarily due to the inherent complexities of representing and manipulating quantum information. This work proposes a method that leverages quantum state reordering to achieve more effective data reduction. The core idea involves encoding quantum data into specific quantum states and subsequently applying reordering algorithms designed to exploit redundancies within the encoded states. This approach aligns with fundamental quantum information theory and provides a potentially more efficient pathway to compressing quantum data, reducing storage and transmission requirements. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key components, including state encoding, reordering algorithm design, and compression performance analysis. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of this technique for future quantum data management systems.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Variable Transverse Field Array
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing quantum gate performance within a variable transverse field array (VTA). The core concept revolves around a dynamically adaptive system capable of monitoring and adjusting its quantum gate parameters in real-time. This is achieved through a feedback control mechanism utilizing quantum measurement results to iteratively refine gate parameters. The proposed method overcomes the limitations of traditional fixed-parameter quantum gates, offering the potential for significantly enhanced quantum computation efficiency and accuracy. The theoretical framework is established, outlining the mathematical principles and algorithms involved. The system's ability to continuously adapt to noise and environmental fluctuations is a key element, promising improved gate fidelity. The ultimate goal is to provide a foundation for high-precision quantum computing applications. The algorithm presented is a gradient-based optimization method tailored for the unique characteristics of quantum gate dynamics. Specifically, we define a cost function that quantifies the gate's performance and iteratively adjust the transverse field strength (si) using a local optimization strategy. The core of the adaptive system is the feedback loop, where measurements are performed, the cost function is evaluated, and the transverse field strengths are updated.

title: 基于多智能体学习的分布式系统设计 (Multi-Agent Learning-Based Distributed System Design - MALDSD)
abstract: This paper explores the application of Multi-Agent Learning (MAL) to the design of distributed systems. Traditional distributed system design methodologies heavily rely on human expertise and often struggle to adapt to complex and dynamic environments. We propose a novel approach, Multi-Agent Learning-Based Distributed System Design (MALDSD), which frames the design problem as a multi-agent learning task. This allows for the automated and adaptive design of distributed systems, leveraging the inherent capabilities of MAL algorithms to optimize for efficiency and reliability. The core claim of this work is that MAL can significantly improve the design of distributed systems. We detail the core mechanism of translating the design problem into an agent-based learning environment, utilizing MAL algorithms for iterative design and optimization. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework and outline future research directions. The key innovation lies in shifting from a centralized, human-driven design process to a decentralized, learning-driven one. This paper aims to establish a foundation for further research and development in this promising area.

title: Formal Language Theory for Interpreting Neural Network Activation Patterns
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to interpreting neural network activation patterns by leveraging formal language theory. Traditional methods often treat neural networks as 'black boxes,' offering limited insight into their internal computations. We posit that the activations generated by a neural network, when considered as a sequence of symbols, can be analyzed using automata theory and formal grammars. This framework allows us to identify recurring patterns, grammatical structures, and potentially discern underlying computational rules governing the network's behavior. The core of the approach involves transforming network activations into strings and applying formal language tools to analyze these strings. This research aims to provide a rigorous, mathematically grounded methodology for understanding the complex dynamics within neural networks, moving beyond purely empirical observations. The paper outlines the theoretical foundations, presents a specific formalism, and discusses potential applications.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Logical Inference on Neural Representations
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to complex reasoning tasks by integrating neural networks with logical inference engines. Traditional neural networks often falter when confronted with problems requiring symbolic reasoning, such as deductive logic. We propose a neuro-symbolic system designed to overcome this limitation. The system learns robust neural representations of data and then leverages a symbolic inference engine to perform logical deductions. Our core claim is that the combination of these two approaches – the representational power of neural networks and the precise reasoning capabilities of symbolic logic – represents a significant step forward in artificial intelligence. We detail the architecture of the system, focusing on the learning process of the neural representations and the integration with a rule-based inference engine. The system is evaluated on a series of logical inference problems, demonstrating its ability to outperform purely neural or purely symbolic approaches. We introduce a new framework for neuro-symbolic reasoning, offering a pathway to more robust and explainable AI systems.

title: ##基于认知架构的机器人控制
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to robot control based on cognitive architectures, aiming to emulate human-like thinking and decision-making processes in robotic systems. The core idea is to construct a robot control system that mimics the human cognitive cycle – perception, memory, reasoning, and action. This is achieved by building a cognitive architecture and integrating it into the robot's control loop. The research addresses the limitations of traditional robot control methods, which often rely on explicit programming and lack adaptability to unforeseen circumstances. By incorporating cognitive elements, robots can exhibit more robust, flexible, and intelligent behavior. This work explores the theoretical framework and key components of such a system, highlighting the potential for significantly advancing robot autonomy and interaction capabilities. The central contribution lies in the design principles and implementation strategies for translating human cognitive processes into actionable control commands for a robotic agent. The proposed system represents a shift from reactive control to proactive, goal-oriented behavior, paving the way for robots that can truly understand and respond to their environment.

title: Event logic graph-augmented generation for interpretable urban waterlogging emergency decision-making
abstract: Urban waterlogging emergency assessment requires credible causal tracing, factual grounding, and actionable response planning. However, directly applying mainstream Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methods to this high-reliability scenario still faces challenges, because similarity-oriented retrieval may retrieve semantically relevant but causally incomplete fragments, providing insufficient support for traceable emergency decision-making. To address this problem, this paper proposes an Event Logic Graph-Augmented Generation (ELGAG) framework. ELGAG constructs an urban waterlogging Event Logic Graph (ELG) to organize historical cases, causal factors, response actions, responsible entities, and emergency resources into event-centered evidence chains. Based on the ELG, a multi-constraint matching and causal aggregation retrieval (MCM-CAR) algorithm is designed to match current emergency queries with historical events and aggregate structured cause–event–response evidence for report generation. A Large Language Model (LLM) then generates emergency assessment reports under domain knowledge-enhanced prompt constraints, while a validation-gated feedback mechanism supports controlled knowledge evolution. Experiments on Guangzhou urban waterlogging data from 2010 to 2019 show that ELGAG achieves a Weighted Overall Quality Score (WOQS) of 0.775 ± 0.001 over five repeated runs and obtains the highest overall performance among vector-based and graph-enhanced RAG baselines under the same evaluation protocol. Ablation, robustness, sensitivity, feedback-update, and LLM-backbone analyses further indicate that the performance gain mainly comes from event-logic representation, MCM-CAR retrieval, and evidence-grounded generation. This study provides an interpretable and verifiable paradigm for applying LLMs to safety-critical urban waterlogging emergency decision support.

title: Personalized Learning Enhancement Through Fuzzy Logic‐Based Adaptive Educational Systems
abstract: Within the scope of this research work, the implementation of fuzzy logic-based adaptive educational systems to improve substantiated literacy tests is investigated. Taking into account the preferences and requirements of individual students in terms of literacy offers a significant problem in today's diverse educational landscape. A flexible and adaptable approach to modeling and logic with squishy and uncertain data is provided by fuzzy logic, which makes it an excellent choice for the development of substantiated learning systems. Within the context of adaptive educational systems, this work investigates the development and implementation of fuzzy logic-based models to tailor literacy content, pace, and feedback to the capabilities and preferences of individual students. It is possible to measure the efficacy of fuzzy logic-based adaptive educational systems in terms of perfecting learning issues and engagement via the use of case studies and empirical analyses. The findings highlight the possibility that these systems would be able to rethink the paradigms that have been used in traditional education by providing adapted literacy strategies that cater to the various needs and preferences of students.

title: Physics-Informed Classical and Quantum Neural Networks for One-Dimensional Schrodinger Eigenvalue Problems
abstract: The Schrodinger equation in one spatial dimension admits a small set of exactly solvable potentials that serve as natural proving grounds for any new eigenvalue solver. We formulate Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and Physics-Informed Quantum Neural Networks (PIQNNs) for the time-independent Schrodinger equation and apply them to three of these benchmarks: the harmonic oscillator, the infinite square well, and the finite square well. In each case a composite loss encodes the differential-equation residual, the normalization condition, the boundary behavior, and the orthogonality between eigenstates, so that the trial wave function is driven toward a genuine eigenfunction without supervised data. The eigenvalues and wave functions returned by both methods are compared against the exact spectra and against three classical references: the matrix Numerov method, the finite difference method, and the shooting method. For the smooth oscillator the two neural solvers reproduce the lowest four eigenvalues to parts per million, while for the square wells they recover the analytic levels with comparable fidelity even where the potential is discontinuous. The quantum circuit, built as a layered angle-embedding ansatz with strongly entangling blocks, converges more reliably than its classical counterpart on the higher excited states, where the loss landscape of the classical network becomes harder to navigate.

evidence.title: Physics-Informed Classical and Quantum Neural Networks for One-Dimensional Schrodinger Eigenvalue Problems
evidence.abstract: The Schrodinger equation in one spatial dimension admits a small set of exactly solvable potentials that serve as natural proving grounds for any new eigenvalue solver. We formulate Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and Physics-Informed Quantum Neural Networks (PIQNNs) for the time-independent Schrodinger equation and apply them to three of these benchmarks: the harmonic oscillator, the infinite square well, and the finite square well. In each case a composite loss encodes the differential-equation residual, the normalization condition, the boundary behavior, and the orthogonality between eigenstates, so that the trial wave function is driven toward a genuine eigenfunction without supervised data. The eigenvalues and wave functions returned by both methods are compared against the exact spectra and against three classical references: the matrix Numerov method, the finite difference method, and the shooting method. For the smooth oscillator the two neural solvers reproduce the lowest four eigenvalues to parts per million, while for the square wells they recover the analytic levels with comparable fidelity even where the potential is discontinuous. The quantum circuit, built as a layered angle-embedding ansatz with strongly entangling blocks, converges more reliably than its classical counterpart on the higher excited states, where the loss landscape of the classical network becomes harder to navigate.

title: Real-Time Musculoskeletal Surrogates for Pediatric Cerebral Palsy: a Credibility Pilot
abstract: Real-time musculoskeletal (MSK) surrogates could support personalized rehabilitation for children with cerebral palsy (CP), but their credibility depends on subject-wise evaluation, low inference latency, and calibrated uncertainty. We develop a subject-conditioned causal neural surrogate using OpenSim-derived static parameters, temporal joint kinematics, true muscle capacities, and training-only perturbations. On a real pediatric CP gait dataset comprising nine children, we use leave-one-subject-out validation on six development subjects and evaluate a frozen configuration once on three locked test subjects. The surrogate accurately reproduces musculotendon lengths (R-square = 0.92 in development validation and approximately 0.95 on locked subjects; nRMSE < 8%) while requiring only sub-millisecond to few-millisecond neural inference, well below a 100 ms interactive-rehabilitation target. In contrast, direct muscle-force estimation remains unstable at this small, heterogeneous scale: pooled metrics can overstate within-subject, per-muscle accuracy. A Monte Carlo credibility pilot further shows that propagating only +/-5% anthropometry and muscle-capacity variation produces severely overconfident nominal 90% intervals (approximately 4% force coverage and below 1% MT-length coverage). These results establish a leakage-free evaluation and credibility framework for pediatric MSK surrogates, while identifying force modeling and epistemic uncertainty as the central next challenges for clinically credible digital twins.
